figures.caption: FIGURE 5 Thermal stability experiments of typical LixPySz sulfide solid electrolytes (SEs). (A) Schematic illustration of the heating apparatus to test thermal stability of sulfide SE, which is sealed in a quartz tube. (B) Experimental photos of typical sulfide SEs Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl at different temperatures. The red box shows the large changes of sulfide SEs at high temperature, which can non- quantitatively reflect the stability of sulfide SEs. (C) i–iii show the X-ray diffraction (XRD) diffraction patterns of Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 at different temperatures, respectively. (D) The differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) test results of Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. (E) XRD, DSC, and thermal stability parameter Th0 values of common sulfide SEs. figures.caption: Fig. 6. Measuring thermodynamic stability and electronic and ionic transport properties of SSEs. Cyclic voltammetry using a) planar current collectors and b) carbon composite electrodes for LGPS and LLZO SSEs (Contains data previously presented in Refs. [1,89]). A schematic of each setup is shown for reference. c) Comparison of two cell conﬁgurations on transport property measurements with mixed conductors. For mixed conductors, electron-blocking layers are needed, as demonstrated by the example d) EIS spectra and e) DC polarization measurements.
